# doit_ps4c_commitment_policies (Data Source)

List all PerfectScale for Commitments (PS4C) commitment policies available to the tenant.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# List all PS4C commitment policies available to the tenant
data "doit_ps4c_commitment_policies" "all" {}

output "policy_count" {
  value = data.doit_ps4c_commitment_policies.all.row_count
}

output "policies" {
  value = data.doit_ps4c_commitment_policies.all.items
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `max_results` (Number) The maximum number of items to return. Setting it reads a single page and returns the `page_token` of the next one; omit it to fetch every page.
- `page_token` (String) Token of the page to start at. With `max_results` set, a single page is read and `page_token` then holds the token of the next page, which is null after the last page. Without `max_results`, every page from this token on is fetched and `page_token` is null after the read. A `page_token` expires. An invalid or expired one fails the read; read again without `page_token` to start over.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))
- `row_count` (Number) The number of items across all pages, as reported by the API. It is the same whatever `max_results` and `page_token` are, so with either set it can be larger than the number of items returned. If the API reports no count, `row_count` is the number of items this read returned instead.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `bootstrap_percent` (Number) Share of the target commitment purchased in the first (immediate) step, as a percentage.
- `id` (String) Policy identifier. Built-in policies use the fixed ids `conservative`, `balanced` and `max_savings`; custom policies have an opaque id.
- `is_built_in` (Boolean) `true` for the three immutable built-in policies, `false` for tenant-defined policies.
- `ladder_step_percent` (Number) Size of each incremental laddering step, as a percentage of the target commitment.
- `lookback_days` (Number) Days of historical usage analyzed to build the recommendation baseline.
- `name` (String) Display name. Built-in names are fixed; custom names are chosen by the tenant.
- `target_coverage` (Number) Share of the optimal commitment the engine aims to purchase, as a percentage.
